사용자 요청 원문:
좋아. 이제 인스턴스를 다시 켜고 첫 태스크를 만들어보자.
필요한 CLI 인증부터 확인하고, 로봇 조립·데이터센터 정비 분야에서 산업 근거가 있고 기존 제출과 겹치지 않는 후보를 골라 제출 전 검토 단계까지 진행해줘.

확정된 제작 조건:
- Category: Impact on AI timelines. 로봇 조립 또는 데이터센터 정비 중 실제 산업에서 자동화할 의미가 있는 물리 조작 하나를 선택한다.
- 제조사 설치·정비 매뉴얼, 공식 조립 절차, 공개 설계, 실제 작업 영상·보고서의 원문으로 작업과 장비 형상·치수·절차를 입증한다. 추측이나 가상 산업 용도를 만들어내지 않는다.
- 여러 후보를 비교하고 목적·물리 기술·성공 조건의 신규성과 로봇의 어려운 조작 능력을 함께 검토하여 하나만 제작한다. 조작의 어려움은 극단적일 필요는 없지만 단순 물체 옮기기를 산업 이름만 바꾼 작업은 피한다.
- 모든 분야의 기존 accepted/pending/open 제출 및 우리 팀 기존 제출, 지정된 기존 벤치마크와 비교한다. 기하·색상·배치·시작 자세·난도만 다른 것은 새 태스크가 아니다. 선정 시점 및 완성 후 다시 전수 비교한다. 불확실한 중복을 통과시키지 않는다.
- 가능한 강체 PhysX 작업을 선택한다. 기존의 검증된 연성 에셋이 없다면 새 연성 솔버 연구는 하지 않는다. 실제 산업 장비의 형태와 중요한 물리 제약을 재현한다. 공개 에셋은 라이선스·출처·치수를 기록하고 적합하지 않으면 직접 제작한다.
- objective와 환경·부품 물리를 먼저 완성·진단한 뒤 YAM 전체 데모·채점기를 연결한다. 물체 순간이동/상태 덮어쓰기로 성공을 만들지 않는다. 관련 부품 파손·금지 동작·실패·부분 점수와 성공 유지 시간을 수치로 평가한다.
- 실제 simulator 측정·두 번의 full-score YAM 데모·실패/부분 점수 대조군·영상/원시 trace 및 깨끗한 경로 재현 검사를 수행한다. 미검증 수치와 성공을 만들어 보고하지 않는다.
- 모든 제작·검증을 마친 후에만 Dream 최종 평가 episode 1회. 실패나 불명 결과도 자동 재평가하지 않는다. 누적 $20 ledger를 준수하고 인증이 없으면 제작을 보존한 뒤 평가 대기한다.
- 결과는 이 run의 새로운 origin 브랜치에 보존한다. 원본 매뉴얼 전체/인증 정보는 공개하지 않는다. 50MB/file 또는 100MB checkpoint 초과는 먼저 보고한다.
- 완료 후 GPU를 stop하고 제출 전 검토 보고서·영상·채점 결과를 제공한다. 실제 미디어 업로드·대회 PR·승인은 하지 않는다.
- 기존 feature/close-snack-bag checkout 및 robocurve-snack-film 인스턴스는 별개 작업이므로 건드리지 않는다.

comparisons.success_condition: Record limits follower movement before reject placement and requires the remaining bins released, ordered and closed up. Candidate requires full transfer with every ball retained and no support separation or jam.
comparisons.reason: Both prevent unintended motion/loss during extraction, but gravity-bin restraint tests sequencing of large containers; the candidate tests continuous microscale support for circulating rolling elements.

comparisons.objective: Administer exactly one eye drop while drawing down a manikin lid and avoiding contact; candidate transfers an LM block.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record coordinates lid displacement with noncontact bottle aiming and force-controlled squeezing. Candidate coordinates jig alignment and bearing-block sliding with ball containment.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires one correctly placed drop, adequate lid opening, no nozzle/eye contact and bottle return. Candidate requires complete transfer, all balls retained and no interface separation, jam, damage or contamination contact.
comparisons.reason: Noncontact liquid dosing and eyelid manipulation are mechanically unrelated to bearing support transfer.

comparisons.objective: Insert a four-fork phase busbar into four circuit-breaker terminals; candidate transfers an uncaged bearing block onto a service jig.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record aligns four forks and pushes them fully home together. Candidate butts a jig to a rail and slides a block continuously across the junction while preserving four circulating rows of loose balls.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires all forks home, hands clear and retention under a 5 N downward tug. Candidate requires complete transfer, all balls contained and no support gap, inclination, jam or damage.
comparisons.reason: Multi-point insertion shares parallel alignment, but final terminal engagement does not test continuous support of freely moving rolling elements throughout a transfer.

comparisons.objective: Place two setting blocks and stand a glass unit on them without touching the sill; candidate transfers an uncaged bearing block.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record positions supports, then bimanually lowers and releases a large fragile pane. Candidate keeps a service jig flush and parallel while sliding a small bearing block across a continuous support interface.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires correct block locations, glass seating, no sill contact and released stability. Candidate requires complete transfer, every ball retained and no gap, jam, impact, contamination or unsafe inclination.
comparisons.reason: Both use supports to prevent damage, but glazing tests placement of a fragile panel onto discrete blocks, not preservation of a rolling-element raceway during transfer.

comparisons.objective: Capture a reference angle with a bevel gauge, carry it unchanged and draw the transferred line; candidate transfers a bearing block.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record adjusts a passive hinge, preserves its angle during transport and guides a marker. Candidate aligns rigid rail/jig profiles and performs force-limited sliding with free-ball containment.
comparisons.success_condition: Record grades reference fit, angle retention, line accuracy/coverage and absence of stray marks. Candidate grades complete block transfer and preservation of every rolling element without separation or damage.
comparisons.reason: Geometric measurement transfer and marking do not overlap with bearing-block support transfer.

comparisons.objective: Install an oversized U-joint cross between yoke ears by inserting one journal, swinging level and recentering; candidate transfers an LM block from rail to jig.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record uses an asymmetric insert–pivot–backslide sequence to place two journals in opposed holes. Candidate uses bimanual end-face mating and a continuous axial slide while preventing free balls from losing support.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires both journals inserted to similar depth, aligned and still. Candidate requires complete transfer, all four ball rows retained, no interface gap/jam/damage and released stability.
comparisons.reason: This record shares constrained insertion and recentering, but it tests rigid cross geometry between opposed holes; it has no continuous support handoff or independently moving elements that can escape.

comparisons.objective: Rout a curved board edge using the starting pin and bearing-guided bit; candidate transfers an uncaged bearing block.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record braces and pivots a board into a cutter, then feeds it safely around a bearing. Candidate aligns stationary support profiles and slides a block across their interface while containing balls.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires routed length and safe feed direction while invalidating off-pin entry, kickback patterns and hand proximity. Candidate requires complete transfer, ball retention and absence of gap, inclination, jam, impact or contamination.
comparisons.reason: Safe cutter engagement and guided material removal do not test rolling-element containment or rail-to-jig transfer.

comparisons.objective: Close a stayed tool-chest lid safely while holding its release.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually hold a spring release and control a hinged lid’s descent while avoiding pinch zones.
comparisons.success_condition: Lid rests shut without excessive speed or pinch-zone entry; release returns home and hands withdraw.
comparisons.reason: The candidate instead mates a jig to a rail and transfers an uncaged recirculating-ball block while preserving continuous support and every ball. Shared bimanual force control does not test the same ability. No missing rubric detail prevents distinction.

comparisons.objective: Safely mount a grinding wheel and its flange/blotter stack on a grinder spindle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Inspect/select parts, align and stack them on a spindle, thread and appropriately tighten a nut.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct undamaged wheel and ordered stack are secured without under- or overtightening; spindle lock is released and hands clear.
comparisons.reason: Spindle stacking and torque control do not require maintaining a flush rail–jig bridge or containing free rolling elements during a sliding transfer. No missing rubric detail prevents distinction.

comparisons.objective: Break a circuit board from its scored panel over a break edge and tray it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align a V-score to an edge, support the panel, and apply controlled bending without twisting the populated board.
comparisons.success_condition: A valid downward break occurs at the score; board is safely placed in the tray and the frame is handled separately.
comparisons.reason: Controlled fracture over an edge is meaningfully different from parallel end-face mating and continuous containment of uncaged bearing balls. No missing rubric detail prevents distinction.

comparisons.objective: Position nickel strip on four battery cells and spot-weld every terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Place a thin strip accurately, manipulate a two-tip welder, and make four localized contacts without disturbing the pack.
comparisons.success_condition: Strip is aligned and bonded at all four cells; welder is returned and the pack remains upright and intact.
comparisons.reason: This tests sequential tool placement and joining, not transfer of a recirculating block across a continuously supported rail–jig interface. No missing rubric detail prevents distinction.

comparisons.objective: Lower a hoisted motor onto four base studs while operating the hoist and steering the suspended load.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinate pendant control with pendulum-load alignment, multi-stud insertion, and pinch avoidance.
comparisons.success_condition: All four studs pass through flat feet, chain is slack, load is stable, controls released, with no strike or unsafe body entry.
comparisons.reason: Although both require bimanual alignment and insertion, the benchmark tests suspended-load steering onto four studs. It does not test a flush sliding bridge, uninterrupted raceway support, or loss-prone free balls.

comparisons.objective: Place a phone, watch, and earbuds case on their respective positions of a three-device charger.
comparisons.physical_skill: Orient and seat three consumer devices so magnetic or contact charging engages.
comparisons.success_condition: All three devices remain released and simultaneously indicate charging.
comparisons.reason: Charging placement tests discrete docking and state activation, not parallel rail–jig mating or containment during block transfer. No missing rubric detail prevents distinction.

comparisons.objective: Locate a hidden wall fastener using a magnetic stud finder.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintain flat sliding contact against a wall until magnetic capture occurs, then release the finder.
comparisons.success_condition: Finder locks to the hidden screw and hangs stably after release.
comparisons.reason: Its sliding is exploratory surface scanning ending in magnetic capture; it lacks end-face bridging, transfer between supports, and freely escaping rolling elements. No missing rubric detail prevents distinction.

comparisons.objective: Sort bottles into a crowded vertical rack without unsafe collisions or loss.
comparisons.physical_skill: Grasp, orient, and insert bottles into constrained rack openings while managing neighboring objects.
comparisons.success_condition: Bottles occupy the required rack positions without drops, breakage, or unsafe disturbance.
comparisons.reason: Crowded object sorting does not test continuous support of an uncaged recirculating mechanism across a flush rail junction. No missing rubric detail prevents distinction.

comparisons.objective: Cap and sort four pens.
comparisons.physical_skill: Match caps to pens, perform axial cap engagement, and place completed pens into designated groups.
comparisons.success_condition: All required pens are correctly capped and sorted, released, and retained in the workspace.
comparisons.reason: Repeated cap fitting and classification are different from maintaining micron-like parallel support while sliding a ball-bearing block between rail and jig. No missing rubric detail prevents distinction.

comparisons.objective: Bleed air from a brake caliper while closing the bleeder before each pedal return.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinate pedal cycling with timed valve opening and closing while controlling fluid flow.
comparisons.success_condition: Air is expelled through valid cycles, the bleeder is shut before every return, and fluid loss or air re-entry is avoided.
comparisons.reason: This tests valve timing and fluid-process sequencing rather than alignment-preserving mechanical transfer and rolling-element containment. No missing rubric detail prevents distinction.

comparisons.objective: Carry a carton whose untaped bottom flaps can open under the load of its cans.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually lift and transport while continuously supporting a failure-prone carton bottom.
comparisons.success_condition: Carton reaches its destination with cans contained and without flap opening, drops, or loss.
comparisons.reason: Both involve continuous support, but the carton task tests gross load support during carrying. It does not require flush precision mating, guided sliding, circulating-ball retention, or an alignment-preserving regrasp.

comparisons.objective: Fit an oxygen regulator to a cylinder or supply fitting.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align the regulator connection, seat its sealing interface, and secure it without cross-threading or damaging the seal.
comparisons.success_condition: Regulator is correctly seated and retained in a safe, leak-resistant configuration.
comparisons.reason: Connector seating and sealing differ from transferring an uncaged bearing block across a continuously butted rail–jig interface. No missing rubric detail prevents distinction.

comparisons.objective: Process a strep-test swab by squeezing its tube, rotating the swab five times, and withdrawing it while maintaining the squeeze.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinate sustained compliant tube compression with counted rotation and constrained extraction.
comparisons.success_condition: Five valid turns occur with the swab head compressed, and withdrawal maintains the prescribed squeeze without spill or loss.
comparisons.reason: Compliant squeezing and swab wringing test deformable-container coordination, not rigid precision alignment or free-ball containment. No missing rubric detail prevents distinction.

comparisons.objective: Immerse a wafer for a prescribed interval using a manual countdown.
comparisons.physical_skill: Handle and immerse a fragile wafer while operating or tracking timing and controlling withdrawal.
comparisons.success_condition: Required immersion duration and handling state are achieved without wafer loss or damage.
comparisons.reason: Timed immersion tests temporal process control and fragile-part handling, not rail-to-jig transfer mechanics. The recovered record supplies enough objective and scoring detail for this distinction.

comparisons.objective: Seat a strut across a keep-out region.
comparisons.physical_skill: Orient and place an elongated structural member into its seats while keeping the member and hands clear of a forbidden zone.
comparisons.success_condition: Strut is correctly supported at its endpoints without keep-out intrusion, collision, or loss.
comparisons.reason: Endpoint seating across a keep-out tests constrained placement, not continuous coaxial support and sliding transfer of an uncaged recirculating assembly. No missing rubric detail prevents distinction.

comparisons.objective: Fasten a bracket bolt using a ratchet where access is confined.
comparisons.physical_skill: Seat a socket, generate incremental ratchet strokes, regrasp as needed, and control tightening in restricted clearance.
comparisons.success_condition: Bracket bolt reaches the specified secured state without tool disengagement, collision, or improper tightening.
comparisons.reason: Confined ratcheting and torque application are different from maintaining a flush support interface while translating a loss-prone bearing block. No missing rubric detail prevents distinction.

comparisons.objective: Sharpen both sides of a kitchen knife on a whetstone and lay it down safely.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintain a 15–20-degree bevel angle during controlled strokes, turn or regrasp the knife, and manage the exposed edge.
comparisons.success_condition: Both sides receive valid sharpening strokes and the knife is released with its edge facing safely away.
comparisons.reason: Angle-controlled abrasive stroking and blade safety do not test rail–jig end-face mating or rolling-element containment. No missing rubric detail prevents distinction.

comparisons.objective: Zero an unpowered robot joint by holding the link at its reference mark and inserting a calibration pin.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually support and finely align a movable link while inserting a pin through coincident holes.
comparisons.success_condition: Joint is on the zero mark, pin is fully seated, assembly is stable, and hands withdraw.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest generic alignment/insertion neighbor, but it tests static hole coincidence and pin insertion. The candidate uniquely tests a sliding transfer over a maintained support seam with four rows of freely simulated balls that may escape.

comparisons.objective: Lay two cables in a cable carrier in the required order and latch every crossbar.
comparisons.physical_skill: Route flexible cables without crossing or riding side plates, then press multiple snap catches closed.
comparisons.success_condition: Both cables occupy every link in order, all crossbars are genuinely latched, ends protrude sufficiently, and hands release.
comparisons.reason: Flexible routing and repeated snap-latching do not exercise flush rail continuation, precision block sliding, or free rolling-element retention. No missing rubric detail prevents distinction.

comparisons.objective: Uniformly heat-shrink a sleeve over a cable lug while rotating the cable and sweeping a heat gun.
comparisons.physical_skill: Coordinate cable rotation with progressive noncontact heating while controlling distance, dwell, and hot-tool safety.
comparisons.success_condition: All sleeve regions recover uniformly with sealed ends, no charring or contact damage, and the switched-off gun is returned safely.
comparisons.reason: This tests distributed thermal-process control, not mechanical support continuity and bearing-element containment. No missing rubric detail prevents distinction.

comparisons.objective: Insert a circuit board fully into an antistatic bag held open by the other hand, then place it in a crate.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually stabilize a compliant bag while feeding a rigid board flat between its layers.
comparisons.success_condition: Board is fully inside near the closed end; bag is released, flat, stable, and wholly inside the crate.
comparisons.reason: Both use one hand to stabilize a receiving element while the other advances a part, but bag opening and compliant insertion do not test a flush rigid support seam or preserve loose circulating balls. The tested failure modes are materially different.

comparisons.objective: Wipe an entire monitor lead once from the plug end toward the clip end without backtracking.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pinch-wipe a free cable while the other hand tensions it, switch roles, and wipe both end bodies outward.
comparisons.success_condition: All required regions are wiped in the permitted directions with no prohibited reverse pass; lead is released on the drape.
comparisons.reason: Directional wiping and taut-cable role switching do not test precision mating, sliding transfer, or containment of an uncaged bearing mechanism. No missing rubric detail prevents distinction.

comparisons.objective: Calibrate a colorimeter with a blank, measure a sealed sample at the requested wavelength, and return both cuvettes.
comparisons.physical_skill: Orient clear cuvette faces, seat vessels in a well, operate lid and controls in sequence, and avoid sample loss.
comparisons.success_condition: A valid blank reference and sample reading are recorded at the requested wavelength; both cuvettes finish released in separate rack pockets.
comparisons.reason: Instrument calibration and cuvette sequencing do not require continuous mechanical support or rolling-element retention. No missing rubric detail prevents distinction.

comparisons.objective: Loosen a nut with an adjustable wrench after snugging its jaw, then remove and set down the wrench.
comparisons.physical_skill: Adjust jaw play on flats, pull in the load-safe direction, and control breakaway torque without rounding the nut.
comparisons.success_condition: Nut turns sufficiently counterclockwise without a loose-jaw or wrong-direction fault; wrench is removed, released, and set down.
comparisons.reason: Jaw adjustment and torque-direction control are different from parallel rail–jig alignment and uncaged-block transfer. No missing rubric detail prevents distinction.

comparisons.objective: Refit a loaded drawer onto roller slides by clearing rear hooks, close it, and pull-test engagement.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually carry a loaded drawer level above riding height, align two runners, lower onto rails, and slide it.
comparisons.success_condition: Drawer is level and engaged on both slides, survives a close-and-release state, then opens to the specified pull-test range without losing its load.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest sliding-support neighbor, but it tests lifting hooks over two rollers and seating a large loaded drawer. It does not require a physically butted end-face bridge, uninterrupted raceway support, or retention of independent balls throughout a block transfer.

comparisons.objective: Seat a sleeve in a housing while registering its radial oil passage.
comparisons.physical_skill: Clearance insertion with axial and angular alignment; preserve sleeve orientation through release.
comparisons.success_condition: Released, supported seating for 1 s within position/tilt limits, with the 10 mm passage unobstructed.
comparisons.reason: Both require alignment-preserving insertion, but this tests radial port registration in a terminal seat. The candidate uniquely tests transfer across a continuously butted rail–jig interface while containing freely simulated recirculating balls.

comparisons.objective: Release a hot air-fryer basket from its drawer and place it on a heat-proof mat.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a release button, lift by the handle, transport, and avoid hot surfaces.
comparisons.success_condition: Basket released on the mat and still, button extended, hands clear, with no hot-surface contact.
comparisons.reason: Button-actuated extraction and guarded transport do not test precision rail-to-jig mating, supported linear transfer, or rolling-element containment.

comparisons.objective: Clip a spring-hinged pulse oximeter fully onto a manikin index finger without dragging the hand.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual hand stabilization, spring-jaw opening, finger alignment, and controlled placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct finger deeply seated at the stop, display up, hand near its mark, device released and still for 1 s.
comparisons.reason: Although both benefit from bimanual stabilization, the oximeter tests compliant clipping onto a finger, not continuous support of an uncaged bearing block across a flush interface.

comparisons.objective: Snap a sip lid completely around the rim of a full paper cup.
comparisons.physical_skill: Circumferential sequential latching with restrained pressing that avoids tipping or crushing the cup.
comparisons.success_condition: All eight lid sectors seated; cup remains undamaged and near its start; hands released and objects stable for 1 s.
comparisons.reason: Distributed rim snapping and thin-container damage avoidance are materially different from parallel rail/jig mating and ball-preserving linear transfer.

comparisons.objective: Stand a lecture gas bottle upright in a bench clamp and lock the clamp.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually stabilize an unstable bottle while sliding a cross bolt and closing a cam lever.
comparisons.success_condition: Bottle upright and centered, bolt home, lever locked, no toppling, released and still.
comparisons.reason: This tests stabilization during clamp actuation. It does not test a moving component crossing a precision support interface or containment of loose internal elements.

comparisons.objective: Disinfect an IV connector for 15 seconds, then attach and operate a flush syringe.
comparisons.physical_skill: Timed frictional wiping, contamination-aware sequencing, fine connector alignment, and plunger actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Full 15 s scrub precedes any syringe contact; syringe is centered/seated and the required plunger stroke completed.
comparisons.reason: Timed cleaning and sterile operation sequencing differ from bearing-block transfer, despite a shared fine insertion primitive.

comparisons.objective: Send a loaded tote down a passive roller conveyor to the far station without a hard impact.
comparisons.physical_skill: Impulse regulation and prediction of rolling motion while preserving an upright load.
comparisons.success_condition: Tote stops at the target station, released and still; bottle remains upright and contained; tote is not lifted or tipped.
comparisons.reason: This tests calibrated ballistic transport on rollers, not contact-maintained bimanual alignment or containment of free bearing balls.

comparisons.objective: Lock a bicycle wheel to a stand using a U-lock.
comparisons.physical_skill: Thread a rigid shackle through spokes and around the stand, then align and seat a crossbar on both legs.
comparisons.success_condition: Lock closed around both rim and stand, both shackle ends engaged, released and still.
comparisons.reason: Multi-obstacle threading and dual-leg closure are different from transferring a recirculating-ball block across a flush, parallel support junction.

comparisons.objective: Open a can using a hand-held rotary opener.
comparisons.physical_skill: Maintain a bimanual clamp while repeatedly regrasping and turning a key around the rim.
comparisons.success_condition: Lid cut completely around; can remains upright; opener removed, set down, and released.
comparisons.reason: This tests sustained clamping plus cyclic rotary regrasping. The candidate instead tests linear sliding while continuously preserving a precision support interface and ball containment.

comparisons.objective: Insert an emergency-stop button through a keyed panel hole and secure it with a rear locking ring.
comparisons.physical_skill: Keyed insertion, front-side stabilization, and coordinated rear-side threading.
comparisons.success_condition: Button seated flush with tab in notch; ring tightened to its specified turn and gap; assembly released and still.
comparisons.reason: This is a plausible alignment neighbor, but its tested outcome is keyed seating and threaded retention. It lacks interface-continuous transfer and the catastrophic loose-ball-loss mode central to the candidate.

comparisons.objective: Fill three drywall nail holes with spackle and strike the patches flush.
comparisons.physical_skill: Load and angle a putty knife, pack material, and regulate scraping depth without tearing paper.
comparisons.success_condition: All holes filled within depth tolerance, minimal proud material, no damaging corner drag, knife set down for 1 s.
comparisons.reason: Material deposition and surface finishing are unrelated to supported rigid-body transfer and rolling-element containment.

comparisons.objective: Press a guarded reset button through a service port using a reach rod.
comparisons.physical_skill: Select, orient, and insert a long tool through a constrained aperture to transmit force.
comparisons.success_condition: Button held at least 5 mm in for 1 s while the rod spans the port with required depth and angle.
comparisons.reason: Tool-mediated button pressing tests reach through a guard, not mating two support profiles or sliding an uncaged bearing block without losing elements.

comparisons.objective: Choose fitting tweezers and peel protective film from a display carrier while stabilizing it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool selection, bimanual carrier stabilization, tab grasping, controlled peeling, and tool return.
comparisons.success_condition: Film fully detached and supported outside the carrier; carrier excursion limited; both tweezers returned; hands clear and objects still.
comparisons.reason: Peel-force control and tool selection differ materially from precision rail/jig butt alignment and continuous bearing-element support.

comparisons.objective: Align and trim a card to length on a guillotine cutter.
comparisons.physical_skill: Card positioning and squaring, guarded handle actuation, and hand-clearance discipline.
comparisons.success_condition: Card aligned and cut with blade down; unsafe hand entry never occurs; card and blade released and still for 1 s.
comparisons.reason: The task tests measurement-guided cutting and safety-zone compliance, not precision component transfer or loose-element preservation.

comparisons.objective: Thread shock cord through a spring cord lock while holding its release button.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually maintain button depression while feeding flexible cord through a constrained passage.
comparisons.success_condition: Cord passes through with at least 40 mm on each side; spring grips it; lock rests on table; hands clear and system still.
comparisons.reason: This is a bimanual feed-through neighbor, but it tests flexible threading through an opened clamp. The candidate tests rigid block sliding across a mated support boundary with free-ball containment and gap/inclination sensitivity.

comparisons.objective: Install a three-pin comb busbar into a row of breaker terminals and tighten every terminal.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequential screw loosening, simultaneous multi-pin alignment/insertion, and torque-tool use.
comparisons.success_condition: All pins home and square, all screws clamp their pins, comb resists a 10 N pull, screwdriver down and hands clear for 2 s.
comparisons.reason: Simultaneous multi-pin insertion and fastening do not test continuous rail-like support or retention of freely moving internal bearing elements.

comparisons.objective: Install round and diamond locating pins, then seat a bracket on the fixture.
comparisons.physical_skill: Select and orient asymmetric locating pins, insert them, and lower a multi-hole bracket without binding.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct pin set home with diamond orientation valid; bracket seated, level, square, released, and still.
comparisons.reason: This is a close precision-assembly neighbor, but it tests terminal multi-pin location. The candidate's defining ability is uninterrupted support during sliding transfer across a flush interface, with any lost ball invalidating success.

comparisons.objective: Move hex nuts from a bin to a tray while recording their count on a mechanical tally counter.
comparisons.physical_skill: Part transfer coordinated with counter reset and repeated key actuation.
comparisons.success_condition: Counter first reaches 0000, final reading matches the released nuts resting in the tray, with no dropped nuts.
comparisons.reason: Counting-state synchronization and repetitive pick-and-place do not exercise precision interface mating or rolling-element containment.

comparisons.objective: Load washable blender parts into a dishwasher while excluding the electrical motor base.
comparisons.physical_skill: Semantic part selection and collision-safe placement into a rack.
comparisons.success_condition: Jug and lid released and stable in the rack; any motor-base entry permanently invalidates success.
comparisons.reason: This tests object classification and selective loading, not aligned transfer across a mechanically continuous support.

comparisons.objective: Press a guarded reset button through a service port using a reach rod.
comparisons.physical_skill: Orient and insert a long bar through a port to operate an inaccessible control.
comparisons.success_condition: Button depressed at least 5 mm continuously for 1 s with the rod through the port at the required depth and angle.
comparisons.reason: The guarded-button task is identical in substance to board-TK-6WKXGD and remains distinct from the candidate's bearing-block transfer and ball-containment ability.

comparisons.objective: Unfold a laptop stand and seat both support rods in the highest-setting slots.
comparisons.physical_skill: Manipulate a passive scissor linkage and independently align two supports into detents.
comparisons.success_condition: Stand fully spread, both rods seated in the highest slots, and complete outline inside the taped rectangle.
comparisons.reason: Articulated-linkage deployment and detent seating do not require a flush transfer interface, continuous support, or containment of loose rolling elements.

comparisons.objective: Remove a drill battery by pressing both release buttons while stabilizing the drill, then place the battery in a tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual stabilization, simultaneous dual-button squeeze, constrained rail sliding, and placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Both buttons pressed together; battery slid fully off and released flat in the tray; drill displacement limited; no drop.
comparisons.reason: This is a meaningful sliding-removal neighbor, but the rail simply guides a latched battery. It does not test butting a separate support jig, preserving parallel end-face contact, or preventing free balls from escaping during transfer.

comparisons.objective: Arrange two bevelled steel coupons for a single-V butt weld with the specified root opening.
comparisons.physical_skill: Part reorientation, bevel recognition, planar alignment, and controlled gap setting.
comparisons.success_condition: Both coupons flat and still, bevels facing, 1.6–3.2 mm gap at both ends, ends aligned, held for 1 s.
comparisons.reason: Static fit-up and gap measurement differ from dynamic sliding across a contact-maintained interface with internal element-loss hazards.

comparisons.objective: Finish rolling paint onto only the bare areas of a partly painted panel.
comparisons.physical_skill: Surface-state perception, roller contact control, complete coverage, and overlap minimization.
comparisons.success_condition: All bare cells painted with limited repainting and no table contamination; full state held 1 s.
comparisons.reason: Coverage planning and coating control are unrelated to precision assembly transfer and bearing-ball containment.

comparisons.objective: Use an insulated fuse puller to rock a target cartridge fuse from its clips and place it in a tray.
comparisons.physical_skill: Tool grasping, target selection, jaw clamping, sequential end-by-end levering, and controlled placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Only F2 is removed while held by the puller and comes to rest in the tray; neighboring fuses remain undisturbed.
comparisons.reason: Sequential levering with a dedicated puller tests extraction from spring clips. The candidate tests insertion-like transfer over a continuously supported rail/jig junction and preservation of all free rolling elements.

comparisons.objective: Gauge and sort seven blocks by dimensional tolerance.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeatedly seat blocks in GO/NO-GO gaps, observe fit, then sort.
comparisons.success_condition: Every block must be validly checked and placed in the correct tray; escapes and false rejects are penalized.
comparisons.reason: The candidate transfers one bearing carriage across a butted rail–jig interface while continuously containing free balls. Gauge-based classification and sorting do not test continuity of rolling-element support.

comparisons.objective: Insert and lock a hose fitting in a sprung quick-connect coupler.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually retract a collar, align and insert a nipple, then release the collar into its groove.
comparisons.success_condition: The fitting must be seated, pawl-engaged, collar-forward, released, still, and able to resist a 10 N pull.
comparisons.reason: Both involve alignment and sliding, but this record tests collar actuation and latch engagement. It does not test a moving carriage bridging two supports or preservation of freely moving bearing balls.

comparisons.objective: Prime an insulin pen and set a 12-unit dose.
comparisons.physical_skill: Remove a shield, orient the needle upward, dial, push against resistance, hold, and redial.
comparisons.success_condition: A valid 2-unit safety shot with visible drop and five-second hold must precede a final 12-unit setting without needle contact or dropping.
comparisons.reason: The tested ability is sequenced dose control and safe needle orientation, not precision rail transfer or continuous rolling-element containment.

comparisons.objective: Flex a printer build plate to release a printed part without kinking the plate.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual symmetric bending under a curvature limit, followed by part placement and plate restoration.
comparisons.success_condition: The part must release and enter the bin while the plate stays above its support, avoids excessive curvature, and returns flat.
comparisons.reason: This tests controlled deformation and adhesive release. The candidate uses rigid rail/jig alignment and must prevent free balls escaping during a supported slide.

comparisons.objective: Fill a narrow-necked bottle with beads using an inferred funnel.
comparisons.physical_skill: Select and seat a funnel, then pour many loose beads through it.
comparisons.success_condition: At least 22 of 24 beads must settle inside the bottle for one second.
comparisons.reason: Although both protect many loose bodies from loss, this record tests tool selection and gravity pouring into a container. It does not require translating an assembly across a gap while maintaining a continuous raceway.

comparisons.objective: Serve one meatball without utensil cross-contamination.
comparisons.physical_skill: Choose the clean scoop, physically support and lift the meatball, then release it on a plate.
comparisons.success_condition: Exactly one meatball must be delivered with the clean utensil and no propagated contamination or spill.
comparisons.reason: The record tests utensil selection, scooping, and contact-history hygiene, not flush rail mating or containment of recirculating elements.

comparisons.objective: Seat an access panel and place two retainer bars across its edges.
comparisons.physical_skill: Fit a panel flush in a pocket, then orient and place bars into rib slots in the required order.
comparisons.success_condition: The panel must be flush and both bars flat, aligned, and overlapping the panel by at least 20 mm.
comparisons.reason: Both include precision alignment, but this is sequential static placement. It lacks a continuous support handoff and any freely moving elements that can escape during transfer.

comparisons.objective: Retrieve an out-of-reach jar by pulling its supporting board, then place it in a basket.
comparisons.physical_skill: Move a support surface without losing its payload, then pick and place the payload.
comparisons.success_condition: The jar must settle in the basket; partial credit only brings it into reach, and falling off the table fails.
comparisons.reason: The shared primitive is moving an object via its support. Here the jar merely rides on a board before an ordinary pick; no aligned support junction, constrained slide, or internal ball containment is tested.

comparisons.objective: Identify a too-heavy carton, shelve the light cartons, and slide the heavy one to a handoff zone.
comparisons.physical_skill: Test-lift visually identical loads, infer mass from resistance, and choose lifting versus sliding.
comparisons.success_condition: Both light cartons must be on the shelf and the test-lifted heavy carton upright on the mat without drops or incorrect handoff.
comparisons.reason: This tests load discrimination and safe fallback behavior, not precision bearing transfer or continuous geometric support.

comparisons.objective: Orient stack-nest totes so they stack on full totes instead of nesting into their contents.
comparisons.physical_skill: Infer asymmetric tote orientation and lower each tote onto load-bearing ledges.
comparisons.success_condition: Both grey totes must rest released on the ledges without descending into or disturbing the parts boxes.
comparisons.reason: Both penalize loss of support, but tote stacking tests orientation-dependent placement onto ledges. It does not require a support-to-support sliding handoff or preservation of free rolling elements.

comparisons.objective: Peel open a sterile pouch and transfer forceps to a sterile drape.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanually peel flexible sheets, release the instrument without touching it, and segregate waste.
comparisons.success_condition: The pouch must be opened, forceps delivered, sheets discarded, and arms withdrawn with no contamination contact.
comparisons.reason: This record tests deformable peeling and sterile contact constraints. The candidate tests rigid alignment, force-limited sliding, regrasping, and ball containment.

comparisons.objective: Load a caulking gun and seal a bath joint.
comparisons.physical_skill: Insert a cartridge, operate the rod and trigger, and coordinate extrusion with tool motion.
comparisons.success_condition: At least 95% of the joint must receive a continuous adequate bead, and the gun must be safely released.
comparisons.reason: The central ability is tool loading plus controlled material deposition. It does not test bearing-carriage transfer across a butted support interface.

comparisons.objective: Measure two level scoops of powdered formula into a bottle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Scoop granular material, strike each scoop level against a bar, and pour accurately.
comparisons.success_condition: Both scoops must be properly leveled, total mass must remain within tolerance, and spills or excess powder fail.
comparisons.reason: This tests volumetric measurement and granular handling; free particles are intentionally poured. The candidate instead must retain every ball within a circulating bearing assembly during a constrained slide.

comparisons.objective: Replace two shelf-edge price tickets while preserving the third ticket and cans.
comparisons.physical_skill: Open a strip, extract thin cards, insert replacements into a narrow channel, and close it.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct new tickets must be seated under their cans, old tickets discarded, strip closed, and cans undisturbed.
comparisons.reason: It tests thin-object extraction and channel insertion with identity matching. It lacks continuous support transfer and rolling-element loss prevention.

comparisons.objective: Rack fifteen pool balls tightly and lift the triangle away without disturbing them.
comparisons.physical_skill: Compress many free balls into a packed array and remove a surrounding tool delicately.
comparisons.success_condition: All prescribed neighboring pairs must be within 0.5 mm, the head ball near the spot, and rack removal must not shift a ball over 3 mm.
comparisons.reason: Both tasks manage multiple free balls and penalize loss of arrangement, but this record tests planar packing and tool withdrawal. The candidate tests containment inside four circulating rows while a carriage crosses a rail–jig seam.

comparisons.objective: Refit a delta-printer arm pair onto an effector's paired ball studs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Align two sockets simultaneously, elastically spread the arm pair, and snap both sockets over balls.
comparisons.success_condition: Both sockets must be centered on one stud pair at the specified sprung width, with the effector flat and both grippers clear.
comparisons.reason: This is the closest insertion-style neighbor, but its defining ability is simultaneous elastic spreading and snap-fit retention onto two studs. The candidate requires maintaining a flush, parallel support bridge while sliding a recirculating carriage without losing any free ball.

comparisons.objective: Scoop more than four beads from a tray into a bowl.
comparisons.physical_skill: Collect several loose spheres in one scoop and transport them without spilling.
comparisons.success_condition: At least five beads must settle in the bowl for one second; lower counts earn partial credit.
comparisons.reason: This tests bulk scooping and transport of loose beads. The candidate's balls remain functional internal bearing elements whose uninterrupted physical containment during rail transfer is the tested outcome.

comparisons.objective: Install a temporary grounding set in the safe ground-first order.
comparisons.physical_skill: Place clamps around bars, tighten eye screws to force, release, and withstand tug tests.
comparisons.success_condition: Ground clamp must be tight before phase contact; both correct clamps must reach 120 N and survive 40 N pulls without touching wrong bars.
comparisons.reason: The record tests safety sequencing, clamp placement, and torque/retention force. It does not test aligned sliding between continuous supports or rolling-element containment.

comparisons.objective: Set a bench grinder's tool-rest and tongue-guard gaps before starting it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Adjust two guarded clearances, clamp the rest, and operate the start control safely.
comparisons.success_condition: Both gaps must fall within OSHA limits without touching, the rest must be clamped, and starting under any unsafe condition fails.
comparisons.reason: This is clearance adjustment and safety interlocking, not transfer of a precision carriage across a mated support seam.

comparisons.objective: Ratchet a tie-down strap taut around a crate and latch it before a deck jolt.
comparisons.physical_skill: Perform repeated ratchet strokes, control tension, close the handle, and release before a dynamic test.
comparisons.success_condition: The strap must reach at least 50 N, the handle must latch, and the crate must remain within tight displacement limits during the jolt.
comparisons.reason: The tested mechanism is cyclic tensioning and dynamic load restraint. It shares force control only generically with the candidate.

comparisons.objective: Join a shelf to a cabinet side using two cam locks.
comparisons.physical_skill: Orient cams open, align and push bolts into them, rotate both cams, and return tools.
comparisons.success_condition: Both bolt heads must be captured, both cams turned at least 120 degrees, the joint gap at most 0.5 mm, and tools released.
comparisons.reason: This tests insertion followed by rotary cam capture and joint closure. The candidate has no fastening operation; its defining challenge is uninterrupted bearing support and zero ball loss during translation.

comparisons.objective: Remove one tissue while leaving the next tissue presented and the light box in place.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize the box bimanually and pull an interfolded deformable sheet with controlled friction.
comparisons.success_condition: First tissue must leave the box and reach the tray, second tissue must remain partly contained and protruding, and the box must finish upright and positioned.
comparisons.reason: This tests deformable frictional extraction and presentation of an interfolded follower. It does not test rigid raceway continuity or rolling-element containment.

comparisons.objective: Remove an obstruction and insert a knife safely into its holder.
comparisons.physical_skill: Clear a blocked path, align a blade to a narrow slot, insert deeply, and release.
comparisons.success_condition: The knife must reach the specified depth and alignment; full credit also requires the toy safely released outside the holder.
comparisons.reason: Both require alignment and insertion, but this record tests obstacle clearing followed by single-object slot insertion. It has no support handoff, parallel rail mating, or vulnerable free internal elements.

comparisons.objective: Level and pin-lock a fallen platform before placing two loads on it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Support and align a hinged platform, insert a pin through three holes, then place loads without contacting a mannequin hand.
comparisons.success_condition: The pin must traverse both walls and lug, platform must be level, both blocks placed, arms clear, and any premature loading or hand contact fails.
comparisons.reason: This tests safeguard restoration by multi-hole pin insertion before loading. The candidate instead tests a translating carriage whose internal balls require continuous rail-to-jig support.

comparisons.objective: Replace a blown DIN-rail fuse with the correctly rated spare and close the correct holder.
comparisons.physical_skill: Select the named carrier, extract and segregate a cartridge, insert a matching replacement, and latch the carrier.
comparisons.success_condition: F2 must contain the KTK-6, close and resist a 4 N pull; opening neighbors or fitting the KTK-10 permanently fails.
comparisons.reason: This is identity-sensitive component replacement and carrier latching. It does not require flush support mating, alignment-preserving regrasping, or containment of freely rolling elements.

comparisons.objective: Load and stack four loose blanks in a narrow vertical magazine; candidate transfers one uncaged bearing block across a rail–jig junction while preserving its balls.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests repeated yaw alignment and top insertion of independent rigid blanks. Candidate tests bimanual end-face mating, continuous race support, and alignment-preserving sliding of a recirculating assembly.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires four flat, centred, supported blanks at rest without mouth jams. Candidate requires a completely transferred block, intact four-row ball containment, continuous support, no contamination or damage, and released stability.
comparisons.reason: Narrow insertion is shared, but the record does not test maintaining a physical support continuum for free rolling elements during transfer.

comparisons.objective: Seat a filled syringe in a pump and bring its driver gently to the plunger; candidate transfers an uncaged LM block from rail to jig.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record requires flange-slot alignment and force-limited driver contact without dosing. Candidate requires bimanual rail–jig butt alignment and supported sliding without losing circulating balls.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires a precisely seated flange and near-contact driver with no historical plunger displacement. Candidate requires complete transfer, every ball retained, no support separation, impact, contamination, or unsafe inclination.
comparisons.reason: Both use delicate alignment, but pump loading tests protected contact with a plunger rather than continuous rolling-element containment across a support junction.

comparisons.objective: Insert and seat a swivelling tie-rod ball stud in a tapered knuckle hole; candidate transfers a bearing block onto a service jig.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests controlling an articulated swinging linkage while aligning and pressing a taper. Candidate tests holding two linear supports flush and parallel while sliding an uncaged recirculating block across their seam.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires taper depth, coaxiality, stillness, release, and clear hands. Candidate additionally depends on uninterrupted support and retention of every freely moving ball.
comparisons.reason: The record is articulated peg seating into a terminal socket; it does not test transfer across a mated support interface or rolling-element preservation.

comparisons.objective: Rinse teeth, evacuate modeled water, and return two tools; candidate performs dry precision bearing service.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests timed bimanual tool trajectories, coverage, suction placement, and cleanup. Candidate tests rigid end-face alignment, force-limited sliding, and containment of free balls.
comparisons.success_condition: Record scores wet coverage, recovery, spill/volume limits, tool return, release, and settling. Candidate scores complete block transfer and intact rolling-element support without loss, contamination, impact, or inclination.
comparisons.reason: The tested mechanisms and outcomes—fluid coverage/evacuation versus supported bearing transfer—are materially different.

comparisons.objective: Hold a self-closing gate while pushing a parcel through to a conveyor; candidate mates a jig to a rail and transfers a bearing block.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests simultaneous gate restraint and planar parcel pushing through an opening. Candidate tests precise coaxial/parallel support mating and controlled sliding of an internally mobile assembly.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires no gate–parcel contact, valid gateway passage, parcel delivery, gate closure, and arm return. Candidate requires complete transfer with no interface gap or lost ball and a stable release.
comparisons.reason: Generic bimanual coordination is shared, but the record does not exercise continuous race support or rolling-element containment.

comparisons.objective: Invert and reinsert an AC disconnect pull-out, close its cover, and padlock it; candidate transfers an uncaged guide block to a jig.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests cover holding, retained block extraction/reorientation/reinsertion, and shackle latching. Candidate tests flush rail–jig mating and straight supported transfer without exposing free balls.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires OFF orientation, closed cover, locked shackle, release, and a 20 N verification while leaving the other disconnect untouched. Candidate requires complete block transfer, continuous support, all balls retained, and no contamination or damage.
comparisons.reason: Although both manipulate a removable block, the record tests reorientation and safety lockout, not seam-crossing support continuity for free internal elements.

comparisons.objective: Move four visually identical, differently weighted crushable cups; candidate transfers an uncaged bearing block.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests payload inference and adaptive grip-force control against slip and crushing. Candidate tests bimanual alignment, force-limited precision sliding, and free-ball containment.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires all cups upright and released on a tray with no buckling, slip, drop, tilt, or forbidden grasp. Candidate requires intact ball inventory and uninterrupted rail-to-jig support through complete transfer.
comparisons.reason: Force care is generic; adaptive gripping of compliant containers is a different tested ability from preserving a bearing circulation system across a support junction.

comparisons.objective: Route a retained cable between posts and seat it in a second clip; candidate transfers an uncaged rigid bearing block between aligned supports.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests bimanual deformable-chain routing, slack management, and clip seating while preserving the first retention. Candidate tests rigid end-face mating and supported linear sliding while containing free rolling bodies.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires both clips seated, ordered cable routing through a marked gap, no joint separation, release, and stillness. Candidate requires full block transfer with all balls contained and no support-interface separation, contamination, inclination, or damage.
comparisons.reason: Both preserve retention during bimanual motion, but cable routing through clips does not test a rigid carriage crossing a flush raceway junction with loose balls.

comparisons.objective: Respond to a high-level alarm by closing an inlet while continuing a color-sorting job; candidate performs bearing-block service transfer.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests attention switching, timed valve actuation, and cube sorting. Candidate tests continuous bimanual geometric alignment and precision sliding.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires closure after alarm but before overflow, valve remaining closed, and correct cube sorting; early closure or overflow is penalized. Candidate requires complete, damage-free transfer with every ball retained.
comparisons.reason: The record's central ability is event-timed process intervention during another task, not support-interface alignment or rolling-element containment.

comparisons.objective: Measure a pin with a digital caliper without force-induced error; candidate transfers an LM block to a jig.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests bimanual part presentation, squareness, gentle jaw closure, and release of the slider. Candidate tests rail–jig butt alignment and controlled block translation across a seam.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires a diameter reading within tolerance, angular alignment, and very low jaw force. Candidate requires complete supported transfer, intact ball inventory, and no gap, inclination, contamination, impact, or damage.
comparisons.reason: Both demand gentle precision, but metrology contact and force-error avoidance are not the candidate's continuous support-transfer ability.

comparisons.objective: Tare a balance and dose granules to 1.00 g behind a draft shield; candidate transfers a bearing block.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests door sequencing, container placement, incremental pouring, and feedback-based mass dosing. Candidate tests bimanual support mating and force-limited mechanical sliding.
comparisons.success_condition: Record scores correct tare state, final indicated mass, closed shield, and absence of spilled granules. Candidate scores complete block transfer with every ball retained and no support gap or contamination.
comparisons.reason: Loose-particle dosing and measurement sequencing are materially different from containing rolling elements inside a translating recirculating block.

comparisons.objective: Screw a corkscrew into a cork and extract it while stabilizing a bottle; candidate slides a guide block onto a jig.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests bimanual stabilization plus helical tool engagement and axial extraction. Candidate tests parallel end-face mating and straight seam-crossing transfer.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires cork engagement/extraction, bottle remaining in its cradle, release, and clearance. Candidate requires complete transfer, continuous support, all balls retained, and no damage or contamination.
comparisons.reason: Bimanual stabilization is generic; helical extraction does not test an uncaged bearing's support continuity.

comparisons.objective: Clamp a marked bar and drill through it safely; candidate transfers an uncaged LM block.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests workpiece restraint, screw-clamp tightening, drill-feed operation, and hazard clearance. Candidate tests precision rail–jig alignment and controlled bearing-block sliding.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires a correctly located through-hole, adequate clamp force, retracted drill, and no unsafe hand proximity or loose-bar event. Candidate requires complete ball-preserving transfer without seam separation or inclination.
comparisons.reason: Machining setup and guarded drilling test different physical abilities and outcomes.

comparisons.objective: Place and center a gasket between spread flanges and insert four bolts; candidate transfers a bearing block across a rail–jig junction.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests planar gasket placement in an occluded gap and repeated vertical bolt insertion. Candidate tests maintaining flush, parallel linear supports during continuous sliding of a free-ball assembly.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires a flat centered gasket and all bolts seated, still, and released. Candidate requires complete transfer with every ball still circulating/contained and no gap, impact, contamination, or unsafe inclination.
comparisons.reason: The record is multi-part placement and peg insertion; it lacks continuity of a raceway and preservation of loose internal elements during motion.

comparisons.objective: Carry an already-threaded opaque collar along a curved protected guide to another support; candidate transfers an uncaged block across a rail–jig seam.
comparisons.physical_skill: Available body evidence indicates changing-view clearance control around a curved guide. Candidate requires bimanual end-face mating, parallel support continuity, and sliding while containing free balls.
comparisons.success_condition: The body states that nonzero credit needs actual threading and stillness, full credit needs target alignment/support/release, and prohibited contact forces zero; the referenced complete numeric rubric and all spec versions are absent from this record. Candidate requires full transfer and intact rolling-element containment.
comparisons.reason: The available evidence suggests a meaningful difference—curved no-contact transport versus seam-crossing support transfer—but the record lacks its indexed specification and numeric contact rubric, so a close shared continuous-guide ability cannot be ruled out confidently.

comparisons.objective: Reload a sprung long-arm stapler and staple two sheets; candidate transfers a guide block to a service jig.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests holding a sprung magazine, placing a staple strip, paper feeding, and press actuation. Candidate tests precise support mating and free-ball-preserving sliding.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires a correctly loaded stapler, sheets stapled and withdrawn, hands released/clear, and settled mechanisms. Candidate requires complete transfer with uninterrupted support and no lost rolling element.
comparisons.reason: Spring-loaded tool reloading and fastening do not test a bearing carriage crossing between continuous race supports.

comparisons.objective: Pour mixed coins from a jar and sort them by denomination; candidate transfers an uncaged bearing block.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests container pouring, perception-based sorting, and planar pushing of thin free bodies. Candidate tests bimanual alignment and constrained sliding of an assembled mechanism.
comparisons.success_condition: Record awards coins wholly inside their denomination frames; wrong, unsorted, or jar-retained coins fail individually. Candidate requires every original ball to remain inside four circulation rows during complete transfer.
comparisons.reason: Handling many loose coins is not mechanically equivalent to preserving internal rolling-element support in a bearing assembly.

comparisons.objective: Remove a worn toothbrush head, discard it, and push-fit a new head; candidate transfers an LM block to a jig.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests one-hand stabilization, axial press-fit extraction/insertion, package opening, and disposal. Candidate tests flush rail–jig alignment and continuous race support during sliding.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires the new head fully seated, worn head in the bin, pack state where applicable, and arm return. Candidate requires complete transfer without any lost ball, support separation, inclination, contamination, or damage.
comparisons.reason: Axial push-fit replacement is a terminal removal/insertion operation, not a continuous supported carriage transfer.

comparisons.objective: Safely depressurize and disconnect a pneumatic push-fitting, then insert a blanking plug; candidate transfers a bearing block.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests valve/lock sequencing, collet depression, flexible-line withdrawal, and plug insertion. Candidate tests bimanual rigid support alignment and contained linear transfer.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires safe pressure history, valve closure or lockout, line removal, seated plug, release, and no unsafe reconnection state. Candidate requires complete block transfer with all balls retained and no support gap or contamination.
comparisons.reason: Despite shared withdrawal/insertion primitives, the record's central ability is safe push-fitting release and blanking, not maintaining a continuous raceway for loose rolling elements.

comparisons.objective: Drive a curved suture needle through a pad and hand it to the other hand; candidate transfers an uncaged bearing block.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests rotation about a needle's curvature, constrained tissue passage, and bimanual handoff. Candidate tests linear support mating, precision sliding, and free-ball containment.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires correct entry/exit slots, no tear, pad press, or drop, then a stable handoff while still threaded. Candidate requires full transfer, uninterrupted support, no lost ball, and released stability.
comparisons.reason: Both preserve constraint during bimanual manipulation, but curved-path needle driving and handoff test a different mechanism and outcome.

comparisons.objective: Seat a loose rack on a pinion so two gripper fingers move evenly; candidate transfers a bearing block onto a jig.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests gear-phase alignment, rack seating, and coupled mechanism actuation. Candidate tests parallel rail–jig mating and straight supported translation without losing balls.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires both racks seated, symmetric finger travel, minimum opening, stillness, and released hands. Candidate requires complete transfer, continuous support, and intact rolling-element inventory.
comparisons.reason: Gear meshing and phase symmetry are not the candidate's rolling-element containment and seam-crossing support ability.

comparisons.objective: Remove a hose gladhand from its dummy, align seals, quarter-turn lock it to the correct trailer coupling, and release; candidate transfers an LM block.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests hose management, face-to-face coupling alignment, seal compression, and twist locking. Candidate tests rail–jig end-face mating and linear supported sliding.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires the correct coupling locked, pull-resistant, hose intact/off the floor, and hands clear. Candidate requires full block transfer with every ball retained and no seam separation, inclination, contamination, or impact.
comparisons.reason: Face mating is shared, but twist-lock hose coupling does not test a translating recirculating bearing's continuous race support.

comparisons.objective: Play a two-hand keyboard passage with simultaneous timing and force-dependent dynamics; candidate performs bearing service transfer.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests rapid bimanual key sequencing, velocity control, note release, and rhythm. Candidate tests slow geometric alignment, contact regulation, and mechanical containment.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires the specified note order, beat, bass duration, velocity contrast, no extra notes, and all keys/hands released. Candidate requires complete damage-free transfer with all balls retained.
comparisons.reason: Only generic bimanual coordination is shared; the tested abilities and outcomes are unrelated.

comparisons.objective: Insert a battery with correct polarity and screw a flashlight cap onto real thread geometry; candidate transfers an uncaged bearing block.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests cylindrical insertion, orientation selection, body stabilization, thread engagement, and sustained rotation. Candidate tests flush support alignment and linear block transfer across a seam.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires correct battery polarity, cap thread engagement and at least 300 degrees of tightening, no forced seating or dropped part, and stillness. Candidate requires complete transfer with every ball contained and continuous support.
comparisons.reason: Threaded enclosure assembly is a different mechanism from maintaining a bearing raceway through a rail-to-jig transition.

comparisons.objective: Move a three-box stack to a shelf in one trip without separating it; candidate transfers an uncaged LM block to a jig.
comparisons.physical_skill: Record tests whole-stack bimanual squeezing, transport, regrasping, and balance. Candidate tests narrow end-face mating, parallelism, and force-limited constrained sliding.
comparisons.success_condition: Record requires the stack never to separate, over-slide, or over-tilt and to stand released on the shelf. Candidate requires uninterrupted rail/jig support and retention of every freely moving ball through complete transfer.
comparisons.reason: Preserving a frictional stack during free-space transport does not test continuous raceway support or internal rolling-element containment.

comparisons.objective: Stop a spinning centrifuge, open it safely, and rack a sample tube.
comparisons.physical_skill: Button operation, safe-state sequencing, lid opening, and tube extraction/placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Rotor stopped before opening; tube removed and left upright in the rack without moving the centrifuge or dropping it.
comparisons.reason: The candidate tests rail-to-jig mating and uninterrupted containment of free recirculating balls during a supported slide, not safe-state sequencing or vessel extraction.

comparisons.objective: Sample a handhole atmosphere before conditionally removing its cover bolts.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hose placement and dwell, alarm-conditioned action, bolt loosening, and bimanual handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Complete a valid 60-second sample; remove both bolts only for clean air, or leave them secured after an alarm.
comparisons.reason: Its defining ability is conditional safety sequencing from a gas-monitor result, whereas the candidate tests continuous mechanical support and rolling-element containment.

comparisons.objective: Transfer an electrode roll using a spindle passed through its core and deposit the spindle ends on rests.
comparisons.physical_skill: Through-core insertion, suspended load carrying, and two-end placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Roll carried only by the spindle, both spindle ends supported, released, stable, and without excessive sag.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve alignment and transfer, this record supports and carries a roll on an inserted tool; it does not bridge two guide surfaces or preserve loose circulating elements during a carriage transfer.

comparisons.objective: Unplug a toaster, hold its extra-lift lever, and remove low toast with wooden tongs.
comparisons.physical_skill: Safety sequencing, sustained lever actuation, bimanual tool use, and extraction.
comparisons.success_condition: Toast reaches the plate while unplugged; unsafe reach-in or moving the metal fork invalidates success.
comparisons.reason: The tested ability is coordinated lever holding and safe tong extraction, not precision rail continuity or loss-free bearing-block transfer.

comparisons.objective: Install a booster-seat tray with both catches locked at the second notch.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual tray alignment, guided sliding, and simultaneous spring-catch engagement.
comparisons.success_condition: Both catches lock in the specified notch, the tray is level and released, and the seat is not displaced or tipped.
comparisons.reason: This is a two-rail latching task. The candidate instead requires a flush temporary rail bridge and continuous support of freely moving bearing balls; no target latch or notch establishes success.

comparisons.objective: Seat a servo horn on a splined shaft at the zero angular index.
comparisons.physical_skill: Small-part grasping, coaxial and angular alignment, and controlled axial pressing.
comparisons.success_condition: Horn seated flush at the zero spline index, stationary, released, and not left on a wrong tooth.
comparisons.reason: Both require precision alignment, but this record tests indexed spline registration and press seating. It does not test maintaining a continuous support path while translating an uncaged recirculating carriage without losing elements.

comparisons.objective: Secure a carton to a luggage cart with a stretched bungee hooked around both frame tubes.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual elastic handling, hooking against tension, and controlled release.
comparisons.success_condition: Both hooks remain home, the cord crosses the carton correctly, and the carton survives a tilt/rock/load test.
comparisons.reason: Its central ability is placing hooks against elastic pull and retaining cargo, not rail-to-jig alignment or free rolling-element containment.

comparisons.objective: Place a shackle around a trailer lug, insert its pin through three holes, and screw it fully home.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual hole alignment, pin insertion, thread starting, and repeated rotational regrasping.
comparisons.success_condition: Pin passes through both shackle ears and lug, threads in, and seats its collar within 1 mm without dropped parts.
comparisons.reason: This tests multi-hole pin alignment and threaded closure. The candidate tests a continuous linear support handoff with loose balls and has no threaded fastening outcome.

comparisons.objective: Move all crackers to a basket while excluding a desiccant packet.
comparisons.physical_skill: Object classification, repeated pick-and-place, and handling stacked small items.
comparisons.success_condition: All six crackers are released and stable in the basket; any packet entry permanently scores zero.
comparisons.reason: The task is semantic sorting with exclusion, not precision mating or preservation of rolling elements during a constrained mechanical transfer.

comparisons.objective: Clear a fragile egg from a trivet before placing a pot on it.
comparisons.physical_skill: Obstruction inspection, fragile-object relocation, and safe placement of a heavier object.
comparisons.success_condition: Egg safely supported elsewhere and pot upright on the trivet, with no damaging pot–egg contact.
comparisons.reason: The tested ability is safe obstruction removal and placement; it lacks a continuous guide interface, sliding carriage, or contained free elements.

comparisons.objective: Hold a nail upright while another arm hammers it into a post.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual/multi-arm fixturing, timing, withdrawal, and collision avoidance around an impact tool.
comparisons.success_condition: Nail driven sufficiently while avoiding arm–arm and hammer–helper contact.
comparisons.reason: This is dynamic cooperative fixturing during hammering, not a supported rail transfer or rolling-element preservation task.

comparisons.objective: Hold a cord taut and cut it safely with a knife.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual tensioning, blade control, safe separation, and deformable-object handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Cord cut while held taut and at safe distances; knife set down without blade contact or dropped objects.
comparisons.reason: Its defining ability is tension-assisted cutting with blade safety, unrelated to rigid guide alignment and bearing-element containment.

comparisons.objective: Carry a full cup around an open laptop and place it on a coaster without spilling.
comparisons.physical_skill: Upright transport, clearance planning, and gentle placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Cup reaches the coaster upright while avoiding the laptop, unsafe proximity, spill proxies, and hard landing.
comparisons.reason: This tests hazard-aware transport and spill avoidance, not precision bridging and continuous internal support of a bearing carriage.

comparisons.objective: Sort colored cubes while yielding both arms during a person's visits to a shared bin.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual sorting, human-aware separation, pausing, and resumption.
comparisons.success_condition: All cubes reach matching mats without either arm entering the bin or violating hand separation during visits.
comparisons.reason: The defining challenge is time-varying human safety in a shared workspace, not mechanical alignment or loss-free component transfer.

comparisons.objective: Post a packet completely through a spring-flap drop-box slot.
comparisons.physical_skill: Grasp selection, flap actuation by the object, constrained insertion, release, and follow-up pushing.
comparisons.success_condition: Packet fully inside and stationary with the flap shut; a packet stuck in the slot fails.
comparisons.reason: This is one-way packet insertion through a flap. It does not require mating two support rails or preserving freely circulating elements across their junction.

comparisons.objective: Crimp a cable lug by inserting a stripped conductor into a barrel, closing a press, then removing and returning the cable.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual conductor insertion and hold-while-actuating a lever; unlike the candidate, it does not mate rail and jig end faces, preserve continuous support during a regrasp, or contain free rolling elements.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires specified insertion depth/alignment at crimp, lever release, extraction and return; candidate instead requires complete block transfer with every ball retained and no support-interface separation, contamination or damage.
comparisons.reason: Both include alignment, insertion and bimanual coordination, but the tested outcomes differ materially: irreversible crimp formation versus continuous four-row bearing support during transfer. Candidate gap, angular and force limits are not numeric, but its ball-retention and uninterrupted-support gates establish the distinction.

comparisons.objective: Pull a stiff sliding window open by its delicate handle without tearing the handle off or damaging the window.
comparisons.physical_skill: Force-limited pulling against velocity-dependent drag through a fragile handle; no precision interface mating, supported block handoff or loose-element containment.
comparisons.success_condition: Scores handle-mediated sash travel, with zero for handle or window damage; candidate requires physical rail-jig contact, parallel axes, full block transfer and retention of every ball.
comparisons.reason: The shared force-limiting primitive is generic. This record tests pacing a resistive slider below a breakaway-force limit, whereas the candidate tests alignment-preserving transfer across a butt joint. Candidate force and angular thresholds are unspecified, but that does not make these objectives plausible duplicates.

comparisons.objective: Bend copper tube to 90 degrees while discovering and compensating for hidden springback.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize a free bender, pull and release its lever, observe irreversible bend set, and iteratively correct for material springback.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires a relaxed 87–93 degree bend, released grippers and no overbend, tipping or loss of the bender; it does not assess rail-jig mating or rolling-element retention.
comparisons.reason: This tests inference and correction of a hidden one-way material response, not continuous support and containment during a linear-bearing transfer. Missing numeric candidate transfer tolerances do not affect the distinction.

comparisons.objective: Seat and hold a push-type grease coupler on a nipple while pumping multiple strokes without leakage, then return the coupler.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual sealed axial seating under push-off force, sustained holding, hose management and repeated lever strokes; no moving block crosses a support junction.
