comparisons.success_condition: Requires four valid pump shots while the coupler remains sealed, no leak, and tool return; candidate requires full bearing-block transfer with all balls retained and no interface gap, contamination or damage.
comparisons.reason: Although both demand aligned contact and continuous bimanual control, the record tests maintaining a pressure seal while remotely pumping. The candidate uniquely tests a translating uncaged bearing whose free elements can escape during support handoff. Candidate numeric seal-equivalent tolerances are absent, but the mechanisms remain distinct.

comparisons.objective: Sever a cable tie beside its head with flush cutters without nicking the cable bundle, then return the tool.
comparisons.physical_skill: Stabilize a bundle while positioning and closing cutter jaws at a safe location; this is guarded cutting rather than flush end-face mating and supported sliding.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires the tie cut and removed, insulation undamaged, bundle retained on supports and cutters returned; candidate instead gates on complete block transfer and preservation of every circulating ball.
comparisons.reason: The only commonality is bimanual damage avoidance. This record tests safe cutting-tool placement and actuation, not continuous support, alignment-preserving regrasp or loose-element containment. Unspecified candidate gap and force thresholds do not suggest duplication.

comparisons.objective: Insert two stemmed glasses through the open end of an overhead rack channel and leave them hanging upside down.
comparisons.physical_skill: Grip fragile thin stems, lift each foot above the lips, thread the stem into an open-ended channel, slide and lower to hang; no bimanual butt-joint maintenance or free internal elements.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires one or two glasses stably hanging with foot, stem and tilt tolerances and no knock-over; candidate requires rail-jig contact, parallel support throughout transfer and retention of all balls.
comparisons.reason: This is the nearest geometric neighbor because both slide an object from an open end along a support channel. However, it tests high-reach placement and suspended seating of rigid stemware, while the candidate tests uninterrupted transfer of an uncaged recirculating bearing across a mated interface. Candidate maximum gap and angular tolerance are unpublished, but ball-loss and interface-separation gates make the abilities meaningfully different.

comparisons.objective: Assemble a copper-pipe compression joint in the correct order and tighten its nut to a safe range with a spanner.
comparisons.physical_skill: Sequential pipe, olive and nut insertion followed by repeated spanner regrasping and controlled rotation; it does not maintain a rail-to-jig support bridge or contain free balls.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires pipe home, olive under the nut, 0.75–1.25 turns past snug, no over-compression and tool return; candidate requires complete linear transfer, all balls contained and no gap, inclination, contamination or damage.
comparisons.reason: Both use alignment and regrasping, but this record tests assembly order and bounded threaded tightening, not continuous support during an uncaged bearing handoff. Candidate numeric force, gap and angle thresholds are missing, without creating meaningful ambiguity here.

comparisons.objective: Select and turn a cabinet hinge's side-adjust cam, verify even closed-door gaps, and avoid harmful decoy screws.
comparisons.physical_skill: Acquire and engage a slotted screwdriver, identify the correct cam, apply rotary adjustment, close the door and inspect reveals; no translational supported transfer.
comparisons.success_condition: Requires even 3–6 mm reveals, at most 1 mm difference, flush closure and release, with zero for latched hinge sag; candidate instead requires mated parallel support, full block transfer and zero ball loss.
comparisons.reason: This tests diagnostic screw selection, rotary tool engagement and visual adjustment of door geometry. The candidate tests bimanual physical bridging and containment of freely simulated rolling elements. Its missing numeric transfer tolerances do not undermine this clear mechanism and outcome distinction.

comparisons.objective: Pipe a joined ridged shell border on a cake.
comparisons.physical_skill: Pressure–motion coordination, repeated material deposition, and clean tool release.
comparisons.success_condition: Specified length and count of connected shells with bounded head, tail, ridge, gap, and cleanliness measurements.
comparisons.reason: This is controlled deformable-material deposition and shape formation, not rigid bearing-carriage transfer or rolling-element containment.

comparisons.objective: Secure a free-standing gas cylinder to a wall bracket with its chain.
comparisons.physical_skill: Chain routing, link hooking, snugness selection, cylinder stabilization, and valve avoidance.
comparisons.success_condition: Chain hooked at the correct height and snugness, cylinder upright against the cradle, released, and resistant to a 10 N pull check.
comparisons.reason: Its tested ability is wrapping and hooking a flexible restraint around a hazardous cylinder; it does not test a continuous guide-surface handoff or preservation of circulating balls.

comparisons.objective: Store a board behind a leaning stack without removing the existing boards.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a spring-closing gap open with one arm while inserting a rigid board with the other.
comparisons.success_condition: Board correctly behind the stack; all boards supported in the rack, released, stable, and never removed.
comparisons.reason: The candidate transfers a recirculating-bearing block across a butted rail–jig interface while preserving free balls. Holding boards aside and inserting another board does not test continuous raceway support or rolling-element containment.

comparisons.objective: Seat two IV-set fitments in sequence without twisting or stretching their connecting tube.
comparisons.physical_skill: Keyed seating and clip insertion while managing a deformable tether.
comparisons.success_condition: Both fitments seated in order; tubing remains unstretched and untwisted; hands clear for two seconds.
comparisons.reason: This tests deformable-line management and sequential keyed seating, not an aligned rail-to-jig transfer with uninterrupted support for loose rolling elements.

comparisons.objective: Load four connector modules into a sprung hinged frame and close it until latched.
comparisons.physical_skill: Repeated small-part placement on narrow supports followed by force-controlled frame closure.
comparisons.success_condition: All modules seated with lugs engaged, frame clicked shut, no forced closure or dropped module, hands clear.
comparisons.reason: The central outcome is retaining several modules during sprung-frame closure. It does not transfer a carriage between collinear supports or preserve freely circulating balls.

comparisons.objective: Align a loose splash-shield panel and fasten it with a push-in clip.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual hole alignment followed by axial insertion through two layers and a sprung catch.
comparisons.success_condition: Panel holes aligned and clip fully home, stable for one second.
comparisons.reason: This is hold-and-fasten insertion through aligned holes; the candidate instead requires continuous rail support during longitudinal carriage transfer and prevention of rolling-element loss.

comparisons.objective: Pull deformable cable from a channel to a marked length.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual handover, visually regulated pulling, and straight cable placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Cable end within the target tolerance, no excessive over-pull, loop, lift, or insufficient retained length, then released.
comparisons.reason: Length metering of a deformable cable does not test flush rail mating, carriage transfer, or containment of independent rolling elements.

comparisons.objective: Determine a gauge's zero error and use it to level a platform.
comparisons.physical_skill: Instrument placement, reference measurement, reasoning over biased readings, and button operation.
comparisons.success_condition: Reference and platform readings completed and true platform tilt within 0.15 degrees.
comparisons.reason: This is measurement-driven calibration and levelling, not contact-maintained mechanical transfer. Its rubric does not include rail continuity or component-loss prevention.

comparisons.objective: Open a hinged panel by holding a spring plunger retracted until its strike clears.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual latch release timing and door pulling against a spring-return mechanism.
comparisons.success_condition: Panel reaches the specified opening angle without forcing or damaging the latch/cabinet.
comparisons.reason: The record tests sustained latch release during hinge motion. It has no collinear support transfer, circulating bearing elements, or interface-gap containment outcome.

comparisons.objective: Unscrew a flashlight cap, remove its battery, and place the parts safely.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual threaded disassembly, tipping an internal cell out, and controlled placement.
comparisons.success_condition: Cap unscrewed rather than forced, battery in bin, cap and flashlight safely set down and stable.
comparisons.reason: Threaded disassembly and gravity extraction are materially different from aligning a service jig and sliding an uncaged bearing block across a continuous raceway.

comparisons.objective: Prove a voltage detector before and after testing a conductor, stopping safely if proof fails.
comparisons.physical_skill: Long-tool handling, button holding, ordered contact tests, and conditional safe response.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct prove-test-prove sequence, or safe withdrawal after failed proof; no premature approach to the bar.
comparisons.reason: This tests procedural verification and conditional safety with an instrument, not precision carriage transfer or rolling-element containment.

comparisons.objective: Receive a terminal block from a person and latch it onto a DIN rail.
comparisons.physical_skill: Force-limited handover followed by aligned snap mounting without moving the loose rail.
comparisons.success_condition: Clean handover and released block latched on both rail lips; human-contact, drop, and rail-motion limits respected.
comparisons.reason: Although both involve a rail and alignment, this record tests human handover plus perpendicular snap-latching. The candidate tests longitudinal support continuity between a rail and jig and preservation of free bearing balls.

comparisons.objective: Align a replacement pipe with an installed pipe and slide a coupling across their joint.
comparisons.physical_skill: One arm maintains collinear end alignment while the other slides a sleeve across the support junction.
comparisons.success_condition: Coupling spans both pipes, replacement pipe remains aligned and seated, then hands release and the assembly stays stable.
comparisons.reason: The central tested ability closely matches the candidate: bimanually align two end-to-end supports and slide a guided component across their junction without opening the interface. Preserving loose balls adds a failure constraint and precision burden, but does not clearly establish a meaningfully different core manipulation ability.

comparisons.objective: Detach ripe tomatoes at their knuckles and place them in a tray without harming fruit or plant.
comparisons.physical_skill: Selective bending fracture, gentle grasping, and damage-aware produce handling.
comparisons.success_condition: Ripe fruit detached at the knuckle and placed in the tray; green fruit, truss, and tomatoes remain undamaged.
comparisons.reason: Selective biological detachment under force limits is unrelated to maintaining a continuous rigid guide during carriage transfer.

comparisons.objective: Saw moulding through at a marked 45-degree cut while holding it against a mitre-box fence.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual workpiece restraint, repeated tool strokes, regrasping, and cut alignment.
comparisons.success_condition: Correct complete cut, with saw returned, moulding removed, and arms reset.
comparisons.reason: This tests sustained sawing and workpiece restraint, not support-to-support sliding or rolling-element retention.

comparisons.objective: Brake a coasting flywheel safely, then remove and tray its hub nut.
comparisons.physical_skill: Hold a brake control until zero speed, avoid stored-energy hazards, then perform threaded removal.
comparisons.success_condition: Wheel stopped without hand contact; nut removed and placed upright; brake released and hands clear.
comparisons.reason: Residual-energy control and subsequent nut removal do not exercise rail-jig alignment or continuous bearing support.

comparisons.objective: Extract a jammed card intact with both hands and resume printing.
comparisons.physical_skill: Symmetric two-hand pulling that prevents skew and tearing, followed by button operation.
comparisons.success_condition: Card removed whole and placed down; resume button pressed; hands clear.
comparisons.reason: Balanced extraction of a deformable, tearable sheet differs from advancing a rigid carriage across a precisely butted guide while containing independent balls.

comparisons.objective: Orient an angle-grinder guard toward the operator and clamp it securely.
comparisons.physical_skill: Release, rotate, and reclamp an adjustable guard while stabilizing the tool and avoiding the disc.
comparisons.success_condition: Guard faces the operator within tolerance, clamp lever flat, grinder unmoved, and hands/tools clear.
comparisons.reason: This is guarded rotational adjustment and clamping, not translational transfer between continuous guide surfaces.

comparisons.objective: Tear a loaded shelf-ready tray's front panel off along its perforation without disturbing the contents.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual stabilization and directionally controlled tearing of packaging.
comparisons.success_condition: Panel completely removed only along the perforation; tray and cans remain stable, upright, and released.
comparisons.reason: Controlled fracture of deformable packaging around a heavy load does not test collinear guide mating or rolling-element containment.

comparisons.objective: Move a tissue-roll stub to the reserve spindle, install a new primary roll, and lock the dispenser.
comparisons.physical_skill: Ordered bulky-part handling, simultaneous release-tab operation, spindle seating, and cover-stay release.
comparisons.success_condition: Both rolls engaged on the correct hubs, cover safely closed and latched, hands clear.
comparisons.reason: This tests ordered spindle loading with sprung releases and cover closure. It lacks continuous rail transfer and loss-prone circulating elements.

comparisons.objective: Unscrew capped needles from syringes and place them in a sharps tray without exposing a needle.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual stabilization and millimetre-scale threaded removal while preserving a friction-fit safety cap.
comparisons.success_condition: Each needle unscrewed and deposited capped; any cap separation invalidates the trial.
comparisons.reason: Both penalize loss of a safety-critical component, but the mechanisms differ: threaded hub removal while retaining caps versus carriage transfer across continuous raceways while containing free balls.

comparisons.objective: Cut copper tube at a mark with a tubing cutter without denting or spiralling the cut.
comparisons.physical_skill: Incremental force regulation, repeated orbital tool motion, and regrasping or handover.
comparisons.success_condition: Tube cut through on-mark and square, remaining round, with hands clear of the cutter.
comparisons.reason: This tests cyclic cutting and feed-force control, not end-face mating and longitudinal carriage transfer.

comparisons.objective: Measure subfloor flatness with a straightedge and wedge and report PASS or FAIL.
comparisons.physical_skill: Place a reference tool, search for the deepest gap, insert a wedge gently, and classify the measurement.
comparisons.success_condition: Straightedge properly supported, wedge at the deepest gap with accurate reading, and correct tag placed.
comparisons.reason: This is physical metrology and classification. It does not require transferring a component between aligned supports or preserving internal rolling elements.

comparisons.objective: Run a two-lane ramp comparison and identify the higher-friction sled.
comparisons.physical_skill: Arrange specimens, operate a release gate, observe stopping distances, and select the result.
comparisons.success_condition: Both valid measurements establish a difference and only the higher-friction sled is placed on the target mat.
comparisons.reason: Experimental comparison and selection are materially different from precision service transfer across a rail-jig interface.

comparisons.objective: Unlock a loose box by turning its key in the unusual direction, then slide the lid open.
comparisons.physical_skill: Bimanual stabilization, torque-direction adaptation, breakage avoidance, and lid sliding.
comparisons.success_condition: Key turned clockwise without shear-pin failure, lid opened sufficiently, and box remains controlled.
comparisons.reason: The sliding occurs only after rotary lock manipulation and does not cross a butted support junction or preserve freely moving bearing elements.

comparisons.objective: Clear objects from a laptop and open its stiff lid without spill, tip, or damage.
comparisons.physical_skill: Safe multi-object relocation followed by bimanual hold-down and lid lifting.
comparisons.success_condition: Objects safely set aside, laptop base stable, and lid opened at least 90 degrees.
comparisons.reason: Obstacle clearing and stabilized hinge opening do not test guided transfer between rail sections or rolling-element containment.

comparisons.objective: Operate a meter test switch in a safe order and insert a current test plug.
comparisons.physical_skill: Ordered knife-switch manipulation, constrained plug insertion, and avoidance of an unsafe circuit state.
comparisons.success_condition: Required voltage and phase-A switches opened in order, plug seated and retained, forbidden switches unmoved, after-release check passed.
comparisons.reason: This tests safety-critical switching order and keyed plug retention. It is not a carriage transfer across aligned continuous raceways.

last_candidate.title: Transfer an uncaged HSR12X LM block onto a removing/mounting jig
last_candidate.objective: Bimanually butt a representative removing/mounting jig against an HSR12X rail, maintain parallel continuous support, and slide the uncaged recirculating-ball block fully onto the jig without losing a ball or contaminating or damaging the guide.
last_candidate.success_conditions: Full success requires physical end-face contact, parallel rail and jig axes, complete block transfer, all initially present balls still contained in four circulating rows, no impact, drop, contamination-zone contact, or unsafe inclination, and a stable one-second release. Safe jig mating and partial transfer may receive partial credit. Any lost ball, block jam, separated support interface, direct pose or velocity write, hidden weld, fixed ball, or collision suppression invalidates full success.
last_candidate.industrial_value: THK’s maintenance instructions prescribe a removing/mounting jig when block removal is unavoidable and require discontinuing use if a rolling element falls out. This makes preservation of the bearing elements an actual service outcome rather than an invented difficulty.
last_candidate.dexterity: One hand must keep a narrow jig physically butted and parallel to the rail while the other advances a small bearing block. The robot must regulate contact and regrasp without opening a gap that lets any freely simulated ball escape.

last_candidate.asset_plan: Author a representative full-scale HSR12XRM fixture using the visually verified A1-194/A1-195 drawings: 20 mm block height, 27 mm block width, 45 mm block length, 12 mm rail width, 11 mm rail height, and the documented four-row cross-section with end returns. Model every ball as an independent rigid PhysX body and preserve four physical circulation paths. Make the jig’s support cross-section continuous with the rail and clearly label its unpublished length, ball diameter/count, groove clearance, maximum transfer gap, and angular tolerance as prototype assumptions rather than THK specifications. Freeze those values before development and test ball circulation and loss, gap and inclination sensitivity, timestep stability, contact-force limits, reset freshness, and deliberate misalignment failures before YAM integration.
last_candidate.risk: The manufacturer drawings establish the selected model’s exterior, rail cross-section, four raceway rows, circulation through end plates, and lack of retention. Exact ball diameter/count, internal groove microprofile, jig length, and service tolerances are unpublished; these are bounded representative modeling assumptions requiring sensitivity tests and must not be presented as an exact THK replica.
